description: Instructional depiction of the incompatible classical shared-time constructions discussed in n94: K and K_1 have displaced origins and each construction uses radius ct. The overlapping contours are competing classical constructions, not a valid relativistic same-simultaneity transformation or two physical centers of one simultaneous wavefront. Authored-space sizes regularize layout and are not new numerical givens. No portrait, semantic artwork, answer, or extra visible annotation.

authoritativeText.text:
① 物理理论中的假设，也叫公设，作用类似于数学中的公理。
它是理论的出发点，不是在该理论内部用逻辑证明出来的结论。
在物理学中，公设概括实验事实，由它推出的结果还要接受实验检验。

当时人们设想存在静止的以太，地球相对它运动，以太就提供了一个优越的参考系。
迈克尔孙实验和其他探测这种运动的实验没有测到预期效应。
这些结果在各自的测量灵敏度范围内是否定的，并不是从逻辑上证明任何以太设想都不可能。

为解释这些否定结果，同时保留以太参考系，人们提出了多种假说。
例如，为解释迈克尔孙实验，有人假设所有物体相对以太运动时都会缩短长度。

爱因斯坦采用了不同的出发点：不为每个否定结果另添一种假说，而把所有惯性参考系遵循相同物理定律作为理论的基础。
这包括力学过程和电磁过程。
这里的平等针对物理定律，不是说不同观察者记录的运动轨迹都相同。

静止和匀速直线运动都是相对于所选参考系而言的，没有哪一个惯性系因此在定律上更优越；
加速运动不属于这个结论。
迈克尔孙实验未测到当时静止以太模型所预言的地球轨道运动效应，在实验灵敏度范围内支持这一出发点，却不是对所有可能现象的普遍证明。

相对性原理是爱因斯坦理论的一个主要公设：**所有惯性参考系中的物理定律具有相同形式**。
自然过程都遵循这些共同的定律，但各参考系测得的位置、速度和轨迹可以不同。

相对性原理要求所有惯性系中的物理定律具有相同形式。
这是把经典力学的相对性原理推广到包括电磁过程在内的全部物理过程。
这种推广是理论采用的公设，不是仅凭经典力学就能逻辑证明的结论。

狭义相对论不仅以相对性原理为基础，还有第二个公设：**所有惯性参考系测得的真空光速相同，不随光源或接收机相对该参考系的运动而改变**①。
它说的是真空中的光速，不是任何介质中的光速，也不是向加速参考系的简单推广。

① 把真空光速与光源运动无关的观点同相对性原理结合起来，可以表述各惯性系共同的光传播规律。
其中，光速与光源运动无关是一项物理输入，不能只凭相对性原理从逻辑上推出。
这样，真空光速在狭义相对论中具有特殊地位。

提出这些公设需要科学上的勇气，因为它们同经典的时间和空间观念明显冲突。
这个冲突需要检查的是经典时空观念的适用范围。

阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦(1879 至 1955)是二十世纪的重要物理学家。
他创立了关于空间和时间的狭义相对论。

他进一步建立了广义相对论，把对时空的研究扩展到涉及加速参考系和引力的情形。
广义相对论是现代引力理论。

爱因斯坦提出了光量子的观点，把光看作由光的微粒，即光子，组成。
他研究布朗运动，为物质结构的分子动力学理论提供了有力的证据。

爱因斯坦也多次公开反对战争。
人们不仅敬重他的科学工作，也敬重他作为社会活动家反对战争的立场。

图 219 中，两个惯性参考系以相对速度 $\vec{v}$ 运动，分别记作 $K$ 和 $K_1$。
当两系的坐标原点重合时，那里发出一个短暂的火花。
先沿用经典时空观念，设两系共用同一个经过时间 $t$，那么两原点相对位移为 $vt$，球面波前的半径为 $ct$。

再要求惯性系 $K$ 与 $K_1$ 等效，并在两系中都采用相同的真空光速。
与参考系 $K$ 联系的观察者把球面波前的中心放在 $O$，与参考系 $K_1$ 联系的观察者则把中心放在 $O_1$。

如果按经典观念把两系在同一时刻看到的波前当成同一个球面，就要求它同时以 $O$ 和 $O_1$ 为球心，这不可能。
这个表面矛盾来自把相对论公设与共用时间的伽利略式经典描述混在一起，不是相对论中有效的参考系变换。

矛盾不在狭义相对论内部，而在于把不再适用于高速运动的经典时空观念继续当成精确规律。
不同惯性系如何确定同一时刻不能照搬经典观念，因此不能用上面的经典构造来否定相对论公设。

① A postulate plays a role in a physical theory like an axiom in mathematics.
It is a starting assumption, not a conclusion proved by logic within that theory.
In physics, postulates summarize experimental facts, and their consequences must be checked against experiments.

Scientists once imagined a stationary ether through which Earth moved, providing a preferred reference frame.
Michelson's experiment and other experiments seeking this motion did not detect the expected effect.

These were negative results within the sensitivity of the measurements, not a logical proof against every possible ether proposal.
Various hypotheses were proposed to explain these negative results while retaining the ether frame.
For example, to explain Michelson's experiment, it was proposed that all objects become shorter when moving relative to the ether.

Einstein chose a different starting point: instead of adding a separate hypothesis for each negative result, he based his theory on all inertial frames obeying the same physical laws.
This applies to mechanical and electromagnetic processes.

Equality here concerns physical laws, not identical trajectories recorded by different observers.
Rest and uniform motion in a straight line are relative to the chosen frame, so neither gives an inertial frame a privileged place in the laws.

This does not erase the distinction between inertial and accelerated motion.
Michelson's experiment did not detect the effect of Earth's orbital motion predicted by the stationary-ether model being tested.
Within the experiment's sensitivity, this supports the starting point rather than proving it for every possible phenomenon.

The principle of relativity is a central postulate of Einstein's theory: **physical laws have the same form in every inertial reference frame.**
Natural processes obey these common laws, although the positions, velocities, and trajectories measured in different frames can differ.

The principle of relativity requires physical laws to have the same form in all inertial frames.
It extends the relativity principle of classical mechanics to all physical processes, including electromagnetic ones.
This extension is adopted as a postulate of the theory, not proved by logic from classical mechanics alone.

Special relativity also has a second postulate: **all inertial frames measure the same speed of light in vacuum, independent of the motion of the source or receiver relative to that frame.** ①
This concerns light in vacuum, not its speed in every material, and is not a simple extension to accelerated frames.

① Combining the independence of vacuum light speed from source motion with the principle of relativity expresses a common law of light propagation in inertial frames.
Independence from source motion remains a physical input, not something proved by logic from the principle of relativity alone.
The speed of light in vacuum therefore has a special place in special relativity.

Proposing these postulates took scientific courage because they conflict with classical ideas of space and time.
This conflict calls for examining where the classical ideas remain applicable.

Albert Einstein (1879 to 1955) was a major physicist of the twentieth century.
He developed special relativity, a new theory of space and time.

He went on to develop general relativity, extending the study of spacetime to situations involving accelerated frames and gravity.
General relativity is a modern theory of gravitation.

Einstein introduced the idea of light quanta, the particles of light called photons.
His work on Brownian motion provided strong support for the molecular-kinetic theory of the structure of matter.

Einstein also spoke out against war on many occasions.
People respect both his scientific work and his opposition to war as a public figure.

In Figure 219, two inertial frames move with relative velocity $\vec{v}$ and are called $K$ and $K_1$.
A brief spark is emitted where their coordinate origins coincide.

First retain the classical idea that both frames share the same elapsed time $t$, so the relative displacement of the origins is $vt$ and the spherical wavefront has radius $ct$.
Then require frames $K$ and $K_1$ to be equivalent and to use the same vacuum light speed.

The observer associated with frame $K$ places the wavefront's center at $O$, while the observer associated with frame $K_1$ places it at $O_1$.
If classical reasoning treats the wavefronts at a shared instant as one and the same sphere, it demands both $O$ and $O_1$ as centers, which is impossible.
This apparent contradiction comes from mixing the relativity postulates with a Galilean classical description using shared time, not from a valid relativistic frame transformation.
Figure 219

The contradiction is not within special relativity, but in continuing to treat classical ideas of space and time as exact laws when they no longer apply at high speeds.
Different inertial frames cannot simply use the classical idea of a shared instant, so the classical construction above does not disprove the relativity postulates.

inventory.description: One composite diagram contains two overlapping, solid circular cross-sections of spheres with equal apparent radii. Their centers are the two axis origins; the second lies to the right of the first. Both circles cross the shared horizontal axis. These are competing classical constructions, not a physically valid simultaneously centered relativistic wavefront.

The left frame has origin O, upward Y, rightward X, and down-left Z. K appears near its upper axis. Its X ray shares the horizontal baseline with the second frame but ends at the earlier right-facing arrowhead.
The right frame has origin O_1, upward Y_1, rightward X_1, and down-left Z_1. K_1 appears near its upper axis. Corresponding frame axes are parallel and have the same positive directions.
A horizontal right-facing velocity arrow extends from the upper region of the second frame toward the right. Its label is v, with a vector arrow in the source typography.

Each origin has an upper-left radius arrow ending on its own circular contour. Each is labelled ct. The radius arrows point outward from the origins. No numeric radius, time, or vt displacement label is visible.
